store.name: Cuffwell
store.voice: Confident, specific and a little dry. Short declarative sentences. We talk in ounces, stitches per inch and wash counts, not adjectives. We say what a shirt is for and how to wear it, and we're allowed one joke per paragraph. Never 'elevated', 'curated', 'timeless' or exclamation marks.
store.story: Cuffwell was started in 2019 by June Ashcombe, a pattern cutter who spent twelve years cutting shirts for other labels and got tired of watching collars cut corners. She rented the ground floor of a former hosiery mill in Hollis Mill, North Carolina, with one cutting table and two sewing machines. Today a workroom of eleven cuts every pattern there and sews the tees, twill and canvas; oxfords, flannels and linen are sewn by two family workshops in northern Portugal, polos and knits in Peru, chambray in Japan. The range is small on purpose: about two dozen things, most of them shirts. The name is a pattern cutter's compliment: a cuff set well. All people and places here are invented for the demo.

policies.refund:
Return anything unworn and unwashed within 30 days of delivery, with its tags on, for a full refund to your original payment method. Returns are free in the US: write to hello@cuffwell.example with your order number and we'll send a prepaid label. From Canada, return shipping is $12, taken from your refund.

Want a different size? Exchanges are free and we ship the new size as soon as your return is scanned, not when it arrives.

Sale items can be returned within 14 days. Socks can't be returned once worn, for reasons we trust you understand.

If a seam fails within two years, send us a photo. We'll repair the shirt, replace it, or refund it: your choice.
policies.shipping:
We ship to the United States and Canada. Orders leave our Hollis Mill workroom within two business days, folded in tissue in a recycled box.

Standard shipping is $8, and free on orders over $150. US orders usually arrive in 3–5 business days, Canadian orders in 5–9. Canadian orders may owe duties and taxes on delivery.

Tee subscriptions always ship free.
policies.privacy:
We keep what we need to send your order and answer your email: your name, email, shipping address, what you bought and your sizes. Payments are handled by our payment provider; we never see or store your card number.

If you sign up for our monthly email, we use your address for that and nothing else, and every email has a one-click unsubscribe. We don't sell or share your information with anyone.

To see, correct or delete what we hold about you, write to hello@cuffwell.example and we'll do it within 30 days.
policies.terms:
These terms apply when you buy from Cuffwell, 214 Spindle Street, Hollis Mill, NC 28799. By placing an order you agree to them.

Prices are in US dollars and include no tax; tax is added at checkout where it applies. We do our best to show colors accurately, but screens vary, and indigo, linen and garment-dyed pieces vary a little from batch to batch.

An order is accepted when we send your shipping confirmation. If we can't fill it, for example because the last of a size sold while you were checking out, we refund you in full straight away.

Subscriptions renew on their schedule until you skip or cancel them from your account, which you can do any time before the next renewal.

Returns and refunds follow our refund policy. These terms are governed by the laws of North Carolina. Questions: hello@cuffwell.example or (828) 555-0162.

art_direction: Cuffwell, a small shirt brand with a clean, editorial look on a plain white website. Real-photo style, never illustration or 3D. LIGHT: soft, even north daylight from one side, low contrast, gentle soft-edged shadows; never flash, hard sun or orange golden-hour glow. BACKGROUNDS: product shots on a seamless very light gray or white studio sweep, matte, with nothing else in frame; scenes against plain white or pale gray walls, pale oak, raw concrete. PALETTE: white, bone, ecru, light gray and charcoal, with the garments' own colors (oxford blue, indigo, olive, rust, navy, tobacco) as the only color; calm, true-to-life, slightly desaturated. GARMENTS: true-to-life cotton, linen, wool and flannel with crisp, visible weave and texture, neatly pressed or naturally creased, well made, buttons and stitching sharp; every garment completely plain. PEOPLE: invented adults only, always cropped at the neck or chin, seen from the chest down or from behind; never a face, never a recognizable person, no tattoos, no jewelry beyond a plain watch. COMPOSITION: generous negative space, the subject centered or placed with clear intent, straight-on or slight three-quarter angles; a 50–85 mm lens look, true proportions, fine natural grain. ALWAYS AVOID: any text, letters, numbers, logos, brand marks, labels, neck tags, hang tags, patches or embroidery, signage, watermarks; clutter and props; saturated or neon color; mannequins, hangers with logos; a CGI look; heavy vignettes.

products.name: Heavyweight Crew Tee
products.description_html:
The tee the rest of the shop is built around. Thick enough to wear on its own, with a collar that lies flat after a hundred washes instead of rippling. If you buy one thing from us, buy this, in every color.

Details

  • Taped shoulder and back-neck seams
  • Double-needle hem and cuffs
  • Tubular body: no side seams

Fabric

7.2 oz combed cotton jersey, knitted on slow tubular machines in North Carolina, so there are no side seams to twist. The collar is a 1x1 rib with a taped back neck.

Fit

Regular fit: straight through the body, a slightly dropped shoulder, and a hem that covers the waistband. Take your usual size. Between sizes, go down for a closer fit.

Care

Machine wash cold with like colors, inside out. Tumble dry low or hang to dry. It was washed before cutting, so it shrinks less than 3%.

products.name: Classic Oxford Shirt
products.description_html:
The shirt Cuffwell started with, and still the one we sell most. A soft collar with a proper roll, a back box pleat, and cuffs set with two buttons so you can wear them loose or close.

Details

  • 3.25 in collar points with a 3 in roll
  • Back box pleat and locker loop
  • Two-button adjustable cuffs
  • Mother-of-pearl-look buttons, sewn with a shank

Fabric

4.5 oz two-ply cotton oxford cloth from a mill in northern Portugal, woven slightly loose so it softens fast and breathes in summer.

Fit

Regular fit: room through the chest and a gentle taper to a curved hem that tucks in and stays tucked. Take your usual size; see the fit guide for chest measurements.

Care

Machine wash warm. Hang to dry and it barely needs an iron; press the collar points if you care, and we think you should.

pages.title: About Cuffwell
pages.content_html:
Cuffwell makes shirts. Tees, oxfords, flannels, overshirts and linen, plus a cap and some socks because we kept being asked. About two dozen things, made properly, and kept in stock for years rather than seasons.

Why shirts

June Ashcombe spent twelve years cutting shirt patterns for other labels and watching the good parts get cut out to meet a price: the collar interlining went first, then the second cuff button, then the extra inch of hem. In 2019 she rented the ground floor of an old hosiery mill in Hollis Mill, North Carolina, bought one cutting table and two machines, and started making the shirt she couldn't buy.

How they're made

Every pattern is cut in our workroom. Tees, twill and canvas are sewn there too, by a team of eleven. Oxfords, flannels and linen come from two family workshops in northern Portugal that we visit twice a year; polos and knits from a knitting mill in Peru; chambray from shuttle looms in Japan. We name every one of them on the product pages.

What we promise

Collars that roll, cuffs that hold, and seams guaranteed for two years. If one fails, we repair the shirt, replace it or refund it. Your choice, no forms.

pages.title: Contact
pages.content_html: A real person answers every email, usually within one business day. For a size question, tell us your chest measurement and the shirt you have in mind, and we'll tell you what we'd wear.

pages.title: Shipping & returns
pages.content_html:
Shipping

We ship to the United States and Canada from our workroom in Hollis Mill, North Carolina. Orders leave within two business days, folded in tissue in a recycled box.

  • Standard shipping: $8, free on orders over $150.
  • US: usually 3–5 business days.
  • Canada: usually 5–9 business days. Duties and taxes may be due on delivery.
  • Tee subscriptions always ship free.

Returns

Return anything unworn and unwashed, tags on, within 30 days of delivery for a full refund. Sale items: within 14 days.

  • US returns are free. Email hello@cuffwell.example with your order number and we'll send a prepaid label.
  • From Canada, return shipping is $12, taken from your refund.
  • Refunds go to your original payment method within 5 business days of the return reaching us.

Exchanges

Free, in both countries. We send the new size as soon as your return is scanned by the carrier, so you aren't waiting a week without a shirt.

Two-year seam guarantee

If a seam fails within two years, send us a photo. We'll repair it, replace the shirt or refund it.

pages.title: Fit guide
pages.content_html:
Our shirts come in three fits, and every product page says which one it is. Measure a shirt you already like, lay it flat, and compare it with the chest measurements below.

The three fits

  • Slim: close through the chest and waist, for wearing under a jacket. Only our Spread Collar Poplin Shirt.
  • Regular: room through the chest, a gentle taper, a hem that stays tucked. Most of our shirts and tees.
  • Relaxed: a full size roomier, cut to layer. Overshirts, jackets and heavy flannels.

The Slub Tee is Boxy: wide and short, made to be worn untucked.

Sleeves

Our long sleeves are cut to end at the base of your thumb with the cuff buttoned. Every shirt has two cuff buttons, so you can take it in half an inch at the wrist.

Between sizes?

Go down in Regular and Relaxed fits, up in Slim. Or email hello@cuffwell.example with your chest measurement and the shirt you want, and we'll tell you.

posts.title: How to roll a sleeve properly
posts.content_html:
There are two good ways to roll a shirt sleeve, and the one most people use isn't either of them. Here is how we do it in the workroom, where sleeves get rolled a hundred times a day.

The quick roll

Unbutton the cuff and the sleeve placket. Fold the cuff back once, so its inside faces out. Fold again, the same width, so the cuff disappears inside a neat band. Stop below the elbow. That's it: two folds, flat, the same width as the cuff.

The workroom roll

For heat, or for work. Unbutton the cuff and pull the sleeve up past the elbow, inside out, until the bottom of the cuff sits just below the elbow. Then fold the bottom up once, so it covers all but the top edge of the cuff. The cuff peeks out above a clean band, and it stays put all day.

What not to do

Don't roll a thin, tight tube up past the elbow. It cuts off circulation and creases the sleeve in twenty places. Don't roll a button-down with the cuff still buttoned. And don't roll the poplin; it's for the days you keep your sleeves down.

Which shirts roll best

Oxford cloth and chambray hold a roll all day. Linen holds it with a few creases. Flannel is too thick for anything but the quick roll.

No face.

posts.title: Inside the cutting room
posts.content_html:
Every Cuffwell shirt starts on one table: thirty feet of maple in the old hosiery mill on Spindle Street. Here is what happens on it.

Laying up

Cloth is laid in layers, up to forty deep, with the grain checked at both ends. Stripes and checks are pinned at every layer so the pattern lines up from the collar to the pockets. A check that doesn't match at the placket is the first thing we'd notice, so we make sure you never do.

Cutting

A shirt is fourteen to twenty-two pieces, depending on the pockets. We cut collars and cuffs by hand with shears, a few at a time, because they're the parts people look at. The body pieces go under a straight knife.

Bundling

Each shirt's pieces are tied into one bundle with its size, color and lot written on a paper ticket, and sent to the sewing room, ours or one of our workshops in Portugal. When the shirt comes back, it's checked against the same ticket: collar points within an eighth of an inch, stripes matched, every buttonhole clean.

What's on the table this month

The January run of the Corduroy Overshirt, in tobacco and navy. Sizes that sold out will be back first.

image.prompt: A long pale maple cutting table seen in perspective in a bright old mill room with tall windows and white-painted brick walls: layers of rust and green checked flannel cloth laid flat, brown paper pattern pieces and steel weights on top, heavy shears and a wooden yardstick, soft daylight. No people.

posts.title: Flannel, explained
posts.content_html:
Flannel isn't a pattern. A lot of people think it means a plaid shirt, but flannel is a finish: cloth brushed with fine wire rollers until the fibers lift into a soft, fuzzy nap. That nap traps air, which is why flannel is warm without being thick.

Single or double brushed

Cheap flannel is brushed on the outside only, so it looks soft and feels like a dishcloth against your skin. Ours is brushed on both sides. It costs more and takes longer, and it's the whole difference.

Three weights

  • 6.5 oz, our Brushed and Solid flannels: a shirt, from October to March.
  • 9 oz, our Heavy Flannel: nearly a jacket. Wear it over a tee.
  • 9 oz quilted, our Shirt Jacket: a jacket that looks like a shirt, good to about 40°F.

Keeping it soft

Heat is what makes flannel pill and shrink. Wash it cold, dry it low or hang it, and it'll be softer in five years than it is today.

story.body:
Our cutting table is thirty feet of maple on the ground floor of an old hosiery mill. Every Cuffwell pattern is drawn, graded and cut there, and every shirt is checked against it when it comes back from the sewing room.

Collar points within an eighth of an inch. Stripes matched at the placket. Two buttons on every cuff. If it isn't right, it doesn't ship.
